methodological_eligibility.evidence_quote: the statistical approach employed with the automobile industry in developing performance-based energy indicators

paper_type.evidence_quote: The model evolved over a period of time, based on comments from industry reviewers and subsequent analyses.

level_3b.evidence_quote: the automobile assembly EPI applies only to automobile assembly plants that housed the painting operation

stage1.notes: Sector is automobile assembly = discrete manufacturing; not on the closed continuous-process Level-3B list, so level_3b=false. paper_type borderline: core contribution is the ENERGY STAR EPI stochastic-frontier model, but it is estimated on a 35-plant/104-obs panel, so multi-case/applied is plausible - flagged for human. ems_standard: ENERGY STAR Guidelines for Energy Management cited but not a formal EMS standard -> coded none.

multi_site.evidence_quote: Data were provided by five companies who volunteered to participate in the study.

country_region.evidence_quote: Only plants located in the United States producing passenger cars, sport utility vehicles, light-duty trucks, and vans were used in the study.

sector_of_activity.evidence_quote: some broad inferences about efficiency in automobile assembly can be made based on the models

type_of_organisation.evidence_quote: Assembly plants were defined to include body weld, paint, and assembly.
